verdicts.note: Explicit platform pledge to defend the tax on income over $1M and capital gains tax and to expand wealth taxes [S2], plus a separate record claim of passing Vancouver's first B&O tax [S3]. Not a lone ESSB 6346 vote; +2/high fits.

Platform is strongly pole_b (lower rent-stabilization cap, social housing, just-cause eviction) [S2], but the city record she cites includes supply measures (MFTE expansion, fee waivers, removing parking minimums 'to let the market dictate') [S3]; +1 reflects the mix.

Applicable: evidence is her legislative platform, not her council record. Several distinct explicit planks (SAFE Act, Keep Washington Working enforcement, deportation legal defense, divesting pension funds from private detention) [S2] plus 'immigrant rights' in the pamphlet [S1] meet 'repeated explicit statements'.

Applicable (State contest; platform evidence). 'Champion the Washington Health Trust to move our state toward a unified system covering all residents' [S2] and 'universal healthcare' in the pamphlet [S1] are pole_b in two sources.

Urges rejection of I-1 and defends comprehensive sex education [S2]; the council resolution [S8] is a body vote, not hers alone, but is consistent. School-governance evidence correctly placed here, not local-control.

Applicable via her legislative platform. Data-center ratepayer protection and energy/water transparency plus building on limits to Flock-style surveillance [S2] are pole_b, but narrow in scope; +1/medium is right, no more.

Not a roll-call case. Campaign video described as setting out 'concerns about' the income tax and a plank against 'unnecessary financial burdens' [S3][S2]; the video's content is known only from the campaign's one-line description, so -1/medium is the ceiling.

Platform plank on holding repeat offenders accountable [S2] plus an op-ed calling for involuntary treatment pathways and accountability for traffickers and dealers [S8]; the treatment-capacity element keeps it at -1 rather than -2.

Checked the cached letter: HB 2266 is, in her words, 'a zoning and siting bill' that limits 'the ability of local governments to restrict those siting decisions' [S6]. Opposing a state preemption of local siting/zoning authority is core local-control evidence under the 2026-10-08 addendum (zoning, state mandates on local governments), not housing or school governance. Her site's 'State policy should reflect local needs, local infrastructure, and local voices' and 'strong local input' [S2] is a second source. -2/medium upheld.
Explicit yes on I-638 [S5]; her stated support for opportunities for transgender students and no position on abortion or gender-affirming care justify -1 rather than -2.
